prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (Morrowick; Transformer Tap Snapshot to Shore Control Room), Main Transformer, export cable to Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere; Export Limit Advisory if capability<dispatch target; applies accepted ceiling). Public grid, port out of scope. Personnel keep safety authority. Turbine: Turbine Controller (Glassfin; validated commands; blocks protection conflicts; Pitch Deviation Notice; safe mode on aux loss), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone (Larkspur; Leading Edge Tile Image). Substation: Export Cable Monitor (alarms to Control Engineer), Fire Detection Panel, Emergency Generator (Foxglove; auto start on aux loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace, used by Substation Operator to verify restoration checks before next step). Substation Operator: switching, clearances, verifies equipment state; accepts instructions only after authorization with Control Engineer. Control Engineer: checks network config; one-action-per-step instructions with hold points; monitors indications match sequence. Modes: Substation Degraded, Grid Constraint (Duty Planner reassesses, revised authorization). Grid Dispatcher: targets, connection restrictions. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard). Alarms safety>protection>export. Shore: SCADA Gateway (Juniper Vale; Session Revocation Receipt to Cybersecurity Gateway), Shore Control Room (Amber Quay; holds last validated limit on grid comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment after switching period logged), Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown; Squall Window Bulletin; Deferred Task Rationale; work period, dependencies), Work Permit Portal (Isolation Boundary Sketch), Personnel Tracking Console, North/South Access Scanner, Operations Radio Console, Warehouse System. Weather Service (forecast), Metocean Buoy, Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record; Visibility Confidence Note; advises Duty Planner). Modes: Weather Hold, Vessel Standby. Vessel Master: Transfer Manifest Addendum, Crew Count Correction; confirms timing, margins. Service Operations Vessel (Recovery Basket Load Sheet); Crew Transfer Vessel. Marine Coordinator: Berth Slot Confirmation; suspends access in unsafe weather. Field Supervisor: verifies authorization, fitness; pauses on deviation; confirms personnel clear before restoration. Crew: PPE/comms checks, closeout after accounting. Electrical Technician verifies isolation, labels. HSE Officer: hazards, controls before switching, muster. Cybersecurity Analyst (Firmware Hash Attestation); SCADA Engineer validates restoration. Duty Planner:

New part:
S538: An export restriction may arise from a grid instruction, a cable condition, or a substation operating limit.
S539: The Duty Planner treats a confirmed restriction as a Grid Constraint until the applicable limit is clarified or withdrawn.
S540: The SCADA Gateway presents current generation, export, and equipment status to the operations team.
S541: Grid Dispatcher receives the Export Limit Advisory and uses it to set the permitted export level.
S542: The Control Engineer verifies the permitted level, its effective time, and any required ramp rate before changing operating targets.
S543: The Fleet Dispatch Console supports coordinated adjustment of turbine output across the affected operating area.
S544: The Control Engineer reduces active power in controlled steps and checks that measured export follows the revised target.
S545: The Turbine Controller applies the accepted output target while retaining its protective control functions.
S546: The Pitch System adjusts blade angle within its operating envelope and does not override local protection limits.
S547: The Converter Cabinet remains within its electrical and thermal ratings throughout the reduction.
S548: The Export Cable Monitor is checked for temperature, loading, and alarm status during the response.
S549: The Offshore Substation operator confirms that export equipment remains within its approved operating range.
S550: The Main Transformer is monitored for loading and temperature, and any abnormal trend is escalated without delay.
S551: The Grid Interface Relay retains its protection settings unless an authorized switching plan requires a controlled change.
S552: The Control Engineer compares actual export with the permitted level and investigates any persistent mismatch.
S553: If the restriction changes, the Duty Planner records the revised operating basis and coordinates updated targets.
S554: The Maintenance Planning Engine is used to review whether the constraint affects planned work or equipment availability.
S555: Turbines are not repeatedly ramped to chase short-lived fluctuations that fall within the agreed control tolerance.
S556: The Nacelle Condition Monitor and turbine alarms are reviewed for signs that curtailment or ramping is stressing equipment.
S557: The Weather Service information is considered when weather conditions may affect operating margins or access decisions.
S558: The SCADA Engineer investigates telemetry gaps or inconsistent measurements before the team relies on them for control decisions.
S559: The Substation Operator reports any substation limitation that could require a lower export target or local equipment action.
S560: The Control Engineer escalates any condition that threatens equipment limits, protection coordination, or safe operation.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
